title: How a Giant AI Model Fits in Your Pocket
description: Quantization, explained with a dial, a mountain and four memory pipes: how 16-bit weights become 4-bit integers and shrink a giant model until it runs on a phone.
topic: Neural network quantization from 16-bit weights to 4-bit integers on mobile hardware

sources.name: Dettmers et al., LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
sources.supports: Quantization trades numeric precision for memory while preserving model quality.

sources.name: Hugging Face Transformers quantization overview
sources.supports: Describes 8-bit and 4-bit weight quantization used to reduce model memory footprint.

sources.name: Frantar et al., GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
sources.supports: 4-bit post-training quantization of large transformer weights with limited accuracy loss.

beats.narration: A top-tier AI model needs more than a hundred gigabytes of memory before it can answer a single question.
Put that on a phone, and the memory runs out before the model even finishes loading.
The fix is not a smaller model. It is a cheaper way to store each of its numbers.
Sixteen-bit floats keep thousands of tiny steps. Four-bit integers keep exactly sixteen.
The shape survives. A smooth surface and a blocky copy still describe the same mountain.
Four memory channels become one, and the data moving into the chip drops by seventy-five percent.
A quarter of the memory, on the device in your pocket, answering in real time.
